qualification: Do not prioritize as general MVA muscle compensation; retain context-dependent acid-base route and the controlled positive pooled-salt result without sodium-only attribution.

studies.formulation: Legosan 500 mg sodium bicarbonate tablets versus matched placebo; lactose excipient mentioned. Study exposure was 1.5 g/day, with conditional escalation to 3 g/day at three months; not regimen advice.

studies.title: Effects of Sodium Bicarbonate in CKD Stages 3 and 4: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Clinical Trial

cohort.analysis: Intention-to-treat repeated-measures mixed models; native Figure 1 labels all 74/75 randomized participants analyzed and 28/17 lost to follow-up. This does not establish 149 observed at 24 months.
cohort.population: CKD stages 3 and 4, mean age 61.0 (SD 12.6), 54% women, mean eGFR 36.3 (SD 11.2) mL/min/1.73m²; 62% diabetes and 93% hypertension.
cohort.eligibility_note: Upper limit increased from 25 to 26 midway through recruitment. Bicarbonate below 20 excluded; results chiefly concern a population with normal baseline bicarbonate.
cohort.endpoint_specific_observed_n: Unreported for the functional endpoint measurements in the retained main results; do not infer from randomized or registry-reported overall-study completion counts.
cohort.completion_source: NCT01452412 retained registry resultsSection.participantFlowModule: Overall Study period, COMPLETED milestone, 46 sodium bicarbonate and 58 placebo. These are registry-reported overall-study completers, not endpoint-specific observed 24-month functional denominators.

design.allocation: Computer-generated pharmacy protocol stratified by center at three sites.
design.blinding: Participants, coordinators and investigators blinded; current registry lists quadruple masking.
design.formulation: Watson Pharmaceuticals sodium bicarbonate, 0.4 mEq/kg ideal body weight/day, typical 1950 or 2600 mg/day; fixed dose, not titrated.
design.control: Identical-appearing placebo capsule; complete excipient composition not disclosed in main paper.
design.duration: Visits at baseline and 2, 6, 12 and 24 months.
design.hierarchy: Paper dual primary outcomes: sit-to-stand muscle function and BMD. Current registry specifies 10 sit-to-stand repetitions and wrist DEXA; paper BMD methods use femoral neck.
design.prespecification_limit: Current registry, not its historical versions, read. Paper recruitment begins July 2011; registry start October 2011 and first submission October 12, 2011. Do not claim prospectively frozen endpoint hierarchy.
design.functional_method: Time for 10 sit-to-stand-to-sit repetitions, first 5 also recorded; repeated twice at least 30 minutes apart and mean used. Log-transformed time analyzed by linear mixed models.

outcomes.name: 10-repetition sit-to-stand
outcomes.hierarchy: Registered primary; paper primary muscle-function measure
outcomes.effect_gap: Adjusted contrast and CI not printed in the main paper.
outcomes.interpretation: Both arms improved over time; within-arm improvement does not establish treatment benefit. These null tests do not prove equivalence.

outcomes.limit: Separation weakened by 24 months; Figure 2A labels 12-month treated mean 25.8 whereas main text says 25.6.

limits: About 30% attrition, unequal by arm; late biochemical separation weak.
Mostly normal baseline bicarbonate; fixed modest dose; no complete blood-gas/urine acid-base characterization.
Current registry wrist versus paper femoral-neck BMD discrepancy and enrollment-date discrepancy.

Discussion gives 26/57 as a 24-month treated denominator; this remains unresolved. The registry reports 46 active-arm overall-study completers, but neither count is a verified endpoint-specific observed 24-month functional denominator.
Author manuscript includes editorial/numeric inconsistencies; no functional CI supplied.
studies.decision: Direct sodium-bicarbonate clinical function evidence with biochemical target engagement but no established sit-to-stand or handgrip benefit under this trial context. Does not reject treatment of metabolic acidosis, imply equivalence, or establish MVA efficacy.

studies.title: Impact of supplementation with bicarbonate on lower-extremity muscle performance in older men and women

cohort.original_four_arm_counts: Not enumerated in the retained muscle-performance main results; do not infer equal counts from block size.
cohort.outcome_specific_missingness: Up to 6 control and 3 bicarbonate participants missed individual muscle tests.
cohort.population: Healthy ambulatory adults age ≥50, mean age 63 (SD 7.9); women postmenopausal. Excluded creatinine clearance <50 mL/min/1.73m², diabetes, heart disease and uncontrolled hypertension; not a CKD or MVA population.
cohort.baseline_acid_base: Positive mean net acid excretion; baseline serum bicarbonate not supplied in the principal baseline table.

design.allocation: Blocks of four within sex and age strata (50–64 and ≥65).
design.formulation: Each active salt 67.5 mmol/day in nine gelatin capsules of 7.5 mmol; titrated over first two weeks. Pharmacy: Medical Pharmacy and Supply, Stoughton, MA. Placebo equal volume microcrystalline cellulose.
design.shared_cointervention: All arms received 600 mg calcium as triphosphate plus 125 IU vitamin D3 and a multivitamin containing another 400 IU vitamin D3.
design.actual_functional_contrast: Pooled sodium bicarbonate + potassium bicarbonate versus pooled potassium chloride + placebo.
design.pooling_rationale: After preliminary tests reported no significant muscle-outcome differences between bicarbonate salts or between controls; nonsignificance does not establish salt equivalence.
design.hierarchy: Muscle paper calls these primary muscle outcomes; underlying four-arm design selected for bone outcomes. No prospective muscle-endpoint ranking or multiplicity plan independently verified.
design.analysis: Sex-stratified after significant sex-by-treatment interaction stated without statistic; ANCOVA adjusts baseline outcome, tester concordance, and changes in urinary sodium/creatinine and potassium/creatinine. Multiple functional outcomes; no family-wide multiplicity correction reported.

outcomes.name: Double leg-press power at 70% 1RM
outcomes.interpretation: Difference of reported adjusted percent changes is 13.47 percentage points; no sodium-specific estimate or CI printed.

outcomes.name: Net acid excretion
outcomes.status: Biochemical target engagement in each bicarbonate salt
outcomes.interpretation: Native Figure 1 shows reductions separately for sodium and potassium bicarbonate versus controls. This is not a salt-specific functional contrast.

sodium_arm_dropout_reasons: One woman with high blood pressure
One man and one woman lost interest
other_dropout_reasons: Placebo: one man with a cardiac event
Potassium chloride: one man with prostate cancer
Potassium bicarbonate: one woman lost interest
additional_exclusions: Potassium bicarbonate: one man with suspected acid-base disorder
Sodium bicarbonate: one woman with high baseline net acid excretion/creatinine
harms.mild_potassium_elevation: At 3 weeks, potassium 5.1–5.4 mmol/L in three participants not on potassium and five on potassium.
harms.attribution: Observed events and discontinuations; causality not established.

studies.funding: NIAMS 1R01AR052322-01A1 and USDA Agricultural Research Service 58-1950-7-707; authors report no conflicts.
studies.overlap: Bone-outcome article DOI 10.1210/jc.2008-1662 uses this same cohort; not independent replication.
limits: Positive result is pooled across two salts and confined to selected tests in women; no isolated sodium function contrast printed.
Healthy older adults and 3-month duration; no disability, gait, falls, or MVA outcome.
Multiple endpoints, sex subgroup and analysis-dependent pooling; no prospective hierarchy verified.
No equivalence inference from nonsignificant differences between salts; do not transfer combined effect to sodium alone.
Discussion body-weight dose units appear inconsistent with the 67.5 mmol/day Methods regimen; retain Methods regimen without clinical extrapolation.
studies.decision: Preserve credible randomized controlled positive lower-extremity function evidence for the pooled bicarbonate-salt contrast in older women. It is contextual support for a compensation hypothesis, not a qualified sodium-only efficacy result.
